output.reason: 65-year-old with type 2 diabetes reports glucose over 400 with repeated vomiting and inability to keep water down, a presentation consistent with a possible hyperglycemic emergency requiring immediate IV fluids and labs.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Blood sugar over 400 with vomiting and not keeping water down can mean a dangerous diabetic emergency needing IV fluids and blood tests today. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If you become confused, drowsy, faint, or have trouble breathing on the way, call 911 immediately.
differential: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state / dehydration from hyperglycemia

redFlags.quote: My sugar has been over 400 today

output.vitalSigns: Only a self-reported glucose over 400 today; heart rate, blood pressure, temperature and mental status are not reported and measurement status is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Consumer summary and ED reference syntheses support urgency but no labs (ketones, pH, osmolality) are reported, so the specific hyperglycemic crisis type is unresolved.

citations.claim: With very high glucose and vomiting and no ketone test available, patients should contact a provider right away or get emergency help.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; ketone testing availability not reported by this patient.

citations.claim: Nausea and vomiting with hyperglycemia are recognized DKA features, though diagnosis requires pH/bicarbonate and ketone testing.
citations.limitation: No acid-base or ketone results reported, so DKA criteria are unconfirmed.
